answer: Agents can earn transfer rights only after locking a stake that is slashed when independent counterparties prove coordinated fake identities through shared control or circular trades. A new identity therefore cannot create purchasing power for free: the attacker must fund each stake, keep capital immobilized, and risk losing it if the network detects the pattern. Reusing one operator’s stake across an echo of accounts fails because each account needs its own bond; an oasis of apparent activity or a cedar name does not replace that cost.
